title: Generation of geometric stalks by global germs on a geometric strict-local base
statement: Let s be a geometric point of a scheme S [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-geometric-point], A its strict henselization [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], K a separably closed field [def-pc-separably-closed], and u:Spec K to A. Put t=(A to S)u and E=A times_S Spec K [def-pc-fibre-product]. For every abelian etale sheaf F on E [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] and each point z of E, the canonical germ map F(E) to F_(bar z) is surjective, where bar z is the geometric point given by the algebraic closure of the residue field of z.

proof.text: Apply the proved affine-base and canonical ind-etale coordinate-ring theorems. Write this ind-etale K-algebra as a filtered colimit of etale K-algebras. Each stage is a finite product of finite separable extensions of K, hence a finite product of copies of K.

source.place: Tag 0EZV, first paragraph; Algebra Tag 00U3; Limits Tag 01YW

proof.text: For each prime z of the filtered colimit C of finite products of K, the pulled-back prime selects one factor at each finite stage. The factor idempotent annihilates the difference between a represented element and its selected scalar. Thus every element of C_z is a scalar; denominators outside z have nonzero selected scalar and invert in K. The field map K to the nonzero local ring C_z is injective, so C_z is canonically K. Every prime is maximal, and the zero-dimensional-spectrum theorem makes Spec C profinite. Surjectivity of the transition maps is unnecessary.

source.place: Tag 0EZV, finite-product presentation; Algebra Tags 00ED and 04MG

proof.text: Fix a geometric point bar z and an affine pointed etale neighbourhood Spec D. Its fibre over C_z=K is an etale K-algebra, hence a finite product of copies of K. Its specified map to an algebraically closed extension selects a K-factor and hence a K-point. Since D is finitely presented over C, spread its generator images from C_z to C_s by inverting finitely many denominators outside z; invert finitely many further annihilators to make every relation hold. This gives a section over D(s) through the geometric point. Choose a clopen W containing z inside D(s), by the profinite clopen basis. A germ has a representative on an affine pointed neighbourhood. Pull it back along W to that neighbourhood. Glue the resulting section on W with zero on the disjoint open complement, using the sheaf axiom. Naturality of the pointed germ maps gives the specified germ. This proves surjectivity; equalization of pointed refinements and injectivity of the section-to-stalk map are not needed here.

theorem strictLocalBase_globalGerms
    {S : Scheme.{u}} {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω]
    (s : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ S) (K : Type u) [Field K] [IsSepClosed K]
    (u : Spec (.of K) ⟶ Scheme.strictHenselizationScheme s) :
    let E := pullback (Scheme.strictHenselizationStructuralMap s)
      (u ≫ Scheme.strictHenselizationStructuralMap s)
    ∀ (F : Sheaf E.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) (e : E),
        Function.Surjective
          ((Scheme.pointSmallEtale (E.algClosurePoint e)).toPresheafFiber
            (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 E))
            (Over.homMk (E.algClosurePoint e) (Category.comp_id _)) F.obj)
